gila-monster.alt: A Gila monster, a heavy lizard with beaded black and orange-pink skin, walking over red rocks and dry grass at night.
gila-monster.caption: A Gila monster. Its venom led to a drug that works like semaglutide, which copies a human hormone.

lab-mouse.alt: A small brown laboratory mouse sitting on the palm of a hand in a blue disposable glove.
lab-mouse.caption: A laboratory mouse. KPV research so far is in cells and animals. No study in people is published.

glp1-body-map.alt: Drawing of the front of a human head and upper body. The brain, the stomach and the pancreas are shown in colour; the rest of the body is a faint outline.

zagreb-medical-school.alt: The main building of the School of Medicine in Zagreb: a glass front that reflects an older building, above a paved square with benches and a small statue.
zagreb-medical-school.caption: The main building of the medical school in Zagreb, Croatia.

fibroblast-actin.alt: Three cells on a black background under a microscope. Fine red threads fill each cell, with a blue centre and small green worm-like shapes.
fibroblast-actin.caption: Mouse cells with their actin threads stained red. Thymosin beta-4 holds single actin units inside cells.

duodenum-villi.alt: A thin slice of gut wall under a microscope, stained purple and pink. Many finger-like folds point outwards from a curved base.
duodenum-villi.caption: The lining of the upper small intestine. Some cells here release the hormone GIP after a meal.

human-pancreatic-islet.alt: A thin slice of pancreas under a microscope. A round cluster of cells stained dark blue, edged with red cells, sits in pale pink tissue.
human-pancreatic-islet.caption: Cells in a human pancreas. Red cells make glucagon. Blue cells make insulin. Retatrutide also acts like glucagon.
